name: minimal-racket
desc: Modern programming language in the Lisp/Scheme family
why: Racket is a serious Lisp with a rich history, though the minimal build is a fairly standard language install.

brief.what_it_is: Racket is a general-purpose programming language in the Lisp/Scheme family. The homepage shows it running small programs in several dialects, including GUI message boxes, Typed Racket, Scribble documents, and Datalog. The minimal Homebrew formula installs the racket and raco executables. The homepage describes a standard library covering GUI, web servers, databases, and math, plus thousands of packages installed with a single command.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames Racket as a language for making languages: programmers build new, domain-specific languages as libraries, and each module can be written in the language that suits it best.
brief.how_it_works: Programmers define new syntax with macros that rewrite custom syntax into Racket expressions or definitions, so new constructs look like ordinary functions when exported from a module. Parsing packages can map any surface syntax, such as commas and braces, onto a parenthesized language that compiles to ordinary Racket through the macro system. DrRacket's IDE hooks are said to work with these new languages too.
brief.install_notes: The brew caveats (supplied with this project's metadata, not from the homepage) say the minimal formula does not include the DrRacket IDE. To add it, run raco pkg install --auto drracket. The full distribution is available as a cask with brew install --cask racket. The homepage offers a Download Racket page and nightly snapshot builds.
brief.standout: Racket's emphasis is on building languages rather than only using them. The homepage highlights that DrRacket can give IDE features such as go-to-definition arrows to a new language built with Racket macros, and it claims to be the first language to support higher-order contracts and safe gradual typing.
brief.status: Maintained, by the homepage's own evidence: it advertises version 9.3 as available and lists RacketCon 2026 in October. I did not see a last-commit date, so this is inferred from the homepage rather than checked against a repository.
brief.caveats: The homepage carries a banner reading 'Important notice: Racket infrastructure compromise.' The fetched text gives no details, so check the notice before installing. The minimal Homebrew build omits DrRacket and the GUI tooling unless you add them. The homepage is promotional and I did not verify its claims about being the first language with higher-order contracts. The scout note calls the minimal build 'a fairly standard language install', which is a fair summary of the install but not a claim I could check here.
quotes: Racket is a mature and stable product.
Therefore Racket is a language for making languages, so that a programmer can write every module in a well-suited language.
Racket is the first language to support higher-order software contracts and safe gradual typing.
fetch_log: https://racket-lang.org/ : fetched and loaded (homepage text, includes the infrastructure compromise notice and version 9.3 announcement). Docs and package pages were linked but not fetched.
